title: Cancellation rate by city
context: Which markets lose the most requests?
task: Return city (driver's city) and cancel_pct = rides with status other than 'completed' / all rides * 100 (1 decimal).
answer: SELECT d.city, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN r.status <> 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS cancel_pct FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id GROUP BY d.city;

title: Who cancels: rider vs driver
context: Split cancellations by who cancelled.
task: Return by_rider, by_driver and no_show = counts of each cancellation status, one row.
answer: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled_by_rider' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS by_rider, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled_by_driver' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS by_driver, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_show FROM rides;

title: Surge share of bookings
context: How much revenue comes from surge?
task: Return surge_pct = completed fare from rides with surge_multiplier > 1 / all completed fare * 100 (1 decimal).
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN surge_multiplier > 1 THEN fare ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(fare), 1) AS surge_pct FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed';

title: Peak vs off-peak fares
context: Peak hours are 08–09 and 18–20.
task: Return period ('peak' if pickup hour in 8,9,18,19,20 else 'off-peak') and avg_fare (2 decimals) over completed rides.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) IN (8,9,18,19,20) THEN 'peak' ELSE 'off-peak' END AS period, ROUND(AVG(fare), 2) AS avg_fare FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY period;

title: Weekday vs weekend volume
context: Does demand shift at weekends?
task: Return day_type ('weekend' for Sat/Sun else 'weekday') and rides count.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN strftime('%w', ride_date) IN ('0','6') THEN 'weekend' ELSE 'weekday' END AS day_type, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY day_type;

title: Rider tenure at first ride
context: Days between signup and first completed ride.
task: Return rider_id and days_to_first_ride (integer) for riders with a completed ride.
answer: SELECT ri.rider_id, CAST(julianday(MIN(r.ride_date)) - julianday(ri.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_first_ride FROM riders ri JOIN rides r ON r.rider_id = ri.rider_id AND r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY ri.rider_id;

title: Drivers with zero rides
context: Onboarded but never dispatched.
task: Return name and join_date for drivers with no rows in rides.
answer: SELECT d.name, d.join_date FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN rides r ON r.driver_id = d.driver_id WHERE r.ride_id IS NULL;

title: Riders who signed up but never rode
context: Activation campaign list.
task: Return rider_id and name for riders with no rides.
answer: SELECT ri.rider_id, ri.name FROM riders ri LEFT JOIN rides r ON r.rider_id = ri.rider_id WHERE r.ride_id IS NULL;

title: Rides with and without ratings
context: Rating coverage per driver.
task: Return driver_id, completed = completed rides, rated = rides with a rating, for every driver with completed rides.
answer: SELECT r.driver_id, COUNT(*) AS completed, COUNT(rr.rating_id) AS rated FROM rides r LEFT JOIN ride_ratings rr ON rr.ride_id = r.ride_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY r.driver_id;

title: Rides above the city average fare
context: Expensive trips relative to their market.
task: Return ride_id, fare and city for completed rides whose fare exceeds the average completed fare in the driver's city.
answer: SELECT r.ride_id, r.fare, d.city FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' AND r.fare > (SELECT AVG(r2.fare) FROM rides r2 JOIN drivers d2 ON d2.driver_id = r2.driver_id WHERE r2.status = 'completed' AND d2.city = d.city);

title: Top-rated driver's rides
context: How many rides did the best-rated driver complete?
task: Return driver_id and rides = completed ride count for the driver(s) with the maximum rating in drivers.
hint: WHERE driver_id IN (SELECT driver_id FROM drivers WHERE rating = (SELECT MAX(rating) ...)).
answer: SELECT driver_id, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND driver_id IN (SELECT driver_id FROM drivers WHERE rating = (SELECT MAX(rating) FROM drivers)) GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Riders who have tipped
context: Generous riders for a loyalty perk.
task: Return rider_id for riders with at least one ride whose rating row has tip > 0.
answer: SELECT ri.rider_id FROM riders ri WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rides r JOIN ride_ratings rr ON rr.ride_id = r.ride_id WHERE r.rider_id = ri.rider_id AND rr.tip > 0);

title: Drivers never rated below 4
context: Consistently good service.
task: Return driver_id for drivers with at least one rating and no rating with stars < 4.
hint: EXISTS for at least one, NOT EXISTS for the bad ones.
answer: SELECT d.driver_id FROM drivers d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rides r JOIN ride_ratings rr ON rr.ride_id = r.ride_id WHERE r.driver_id = d.driver_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rides r JOIN ride_ratings rr ON rr.ride_id = r.ride_id WHERE r.driver_id = d.driver_id AND rr.stars < 4);

title: Cross-city rides
context: Rider and driver from different cities.
task: Return ride_id, rider city (as rider_city) and driver city (as driver_city) where they differ.
hint: Join both riders and drivers and compare.
answer: SELECT r.ride_id, ri.city AS rider_city, d.city AS driver_city FROM rides r JOIN riders ri ON ri.rider_id = r.rider_id JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE ri.city <> d.city;

title: Average stars per vehicle type
context: Do Premier rides get better ratings?
task: Return vehicle_type and avg_stars (2 decimals) from ride_ratings → rides → drivers.
answer: SELECT d.vehicle_type, ROUND(AVG(rr.stars), 2) AS avg_stars FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id GROUP BY d.vehicle_type;

title: Rides per hour online
context: Driver utilisation = completed rides ÷ hours online.
task: Return driver_id, rides, hours (1 decimal) and rides_per_hour (2 decimals). Aggregate rides and shifts separately to avoid fan-out.
answer: WITH rc AS (SELECT driver_id, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id), h AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(hours_online) AS hours FROM driver_shifts GROUP BY driver_id) SELECT rc.driver_id, rc.rides, ROUND(h.hours, 1) AS hours, ROUND(rc.rides * 1.0 / h.hours, 2) AS rides_per_hour FROM rc JOIN h ON h.driver_id = rc.driver_id;

title: Earnings per hour online
context: Driver take (75% of fare + tips) divided by hours.
task: Return driver_id and earnings_per_hour (2 decimals) = (0.75 × completed fare + tips) / hours online.
hint: Three separate aggregates (fare, tips, hours) joined by driver.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(fare) * 0.75 AS take FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id), t AS (SELECT r.driver_id, SUM(rr.tip) AS tips FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id GROUP BY r.driver_id), h AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(hours_online) AS hours FROM driver_shifts GROUP BY driver_id) SELECT f.driver_id, ROUND((f.take + COALESCE(t.tips, 0)) / h.hours, 2) AS earnings_per_hour FROM f JOIN h ON h.driver_id = f.driver_id LEFT JOIN t ON t.driver_id = f.driver_id;

title: Wait time by hour
context: Average rider wait (wait_min) per pickup hour.
task: Return pickup_hour and avg_wait (1 decimal) over completed rides, ordered by hour.
answer: SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS pickup_hour, ROUND(AVG(wait_min), 1) AS avg_wait FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY pickup_hour ORDER BY pickup_hour;

title: Tip rate per city
context: Share of rated rides with a tip, by driver city.
task: Return city and tip_rate_pct = rated rides with tip > 0 / rated rides * 100 (1 decimal).
answer: SELECT d.city, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rr.tip > 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS tip_rate_pct FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id GROUP BY d.city;

title: Drivers with a high driver-cancel rate
context: Drivers who cancel more than 15% of their rides (min 8 rides).
task: Return driver_id, rides and driver_cancel_pct (1 decimal) for drivers with 8+ rides and driver-cancel share > 15%.
answer: SELECT driver_id, COUNT(*) AS rides, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled_by_driver' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS driver_cancel_pct FROM rides GROUP BY driver_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 8 AND AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled_by_driver' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) > 0.15;

title: Riders who used 3+ different drivers
context: Spread of supply per rider.
task: Return rider_id and distinct_drivers for riders with 3 or more distinct drivers.
answer: SELECT rider_id, COUNT(DISTINCT driver_id) AS distinct_drivers FROM rides GROUP BY rider_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT driver_id) >= 3;

title: Drivers above the average bookings
context: Top half of the fleet by revenue.
task: Return driver_id and bookings (2 decimals) for drivers whose completed bookings exceed the average bookings per driver.
hint: Derived table vs AVG of derived table.
answer: SELECT driver_id, ROUND(bookings, 2) AS bookings FROM (SELECT driver_id, SUM(fare) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id) t WHERE bookings > (SELECT AVG(b) FROM (SELECT SUM(fare) AS b FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id));

title: Cities with drivers but no riders, or riders but no drivers
context: Supply/demand imbalance check.
task: Return city values that appear in drivers or riders but not both (symmetric difference).
answer: SELECT city FROM drivers EXCEPT SELECT city FROM riders UNION SELECT city FROM (SELECT city FROM riders EXCEPT SELECT city FROM drivers);

title: All people on the platform
context: One list of names, tagged.
task: Return name and role ('driver' or 'rider') for everyone, drivers first then riders, using UNION ALL, ordered by role then name.
hint: Literal string column in each SELECT.
answer: SELECT name, 'driver' AS role FROM drivers UNION ALL SELECT name, 'rider' FROM riders ORDER BY role, name;

title: Take rate check
context: Platform revenue = 25% of completed fares plus cancellation fees (fare on cancelled rides).
task: Return platform_revenue (2 decimals) = 0.25 × completed fare + fare from non-completed rides.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN fare * 0.25 ELSE fare END), 2) AS platform_revenue FROM rides;

title: Revenue per km by vehicle type
context: Unit economics per fleet.
task: Return vehicle_type and fare_per_km (2 decimals) = SUM(fare) / SUM(distance_km) over completed rides.
hint: Ratio of sums, not average of ratios.
answer: SELECT d.vehicle_type, ROUND(SUM(r.fare) / SUM(r.distance_km), 2) AS fare_per_km FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.vehicle_type;

title: Zero-distance completed rides
context: A completed ride with 0 km is a data error or fraud.
task: Return ride_id, driver_id and fare where status is 'completed' and distance_km = 0.
answer: SELECT ride_id, driver_id, fare FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND distance_km = 0;

title: Rides before the driver joined
context: Impossible: a ride dated before the driver's join_date.
task: Return ride_id, driver_id, ride_date and join_date where ride_date < join_date.
hint: Join drivers and compare text dates.
answer: SELECT r.ride_id, r.driver_id, r.ride_date, d.join_date FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.ride_date < d.join_date;

title: Shifts with no rides that day
context: Drivers online with zero completed rides on a shift date.
task: Return shift_id, driver_id and shift_date for shifts where the driver has no ride (any status) on that date.
hint: NOT EXISTS matching driver_id and ride_date.
answer: SELECT s.shift_id, s.driver_id, s.shift_date FROM driver_shifts s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rides r WHERE r.driver_id = s.driver_id AND r.ride_date = s.shift_date);

title: Duration with fallback
context: Show 0 instead of NULL for cancelled rides.
task: Return ride_id, status and mins = COALESCE(duration_min, 0).
answer: SELECT ride_id, status, COALESCE(duration_min, 0) AS mins FROM rides;

title: Top 3 drivers per city by bookings
context: City leaderboards.
task: Return city, driver_id and bookings (2 decimals) for the top 3 drivers by completed fare in each city (ties by driver_id).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY bookings DESC).
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT d.city, r.driver_id, SUM(r.fare) AS bookings FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY r.driver_id) SELECT city, driver_id, ROUND(bookings, 2) AS bookings FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY bookings DESC, driver_id) AS rn FROM b) WHERE rn <= 3;

title: Days since each driver's last ride
context: Inactive drivers as of 2025-07-31.
task: Return driver_id and days_idle = days from MAX(ride_date) to '2025-07-31' (integer) for drivers with rides.
answer: SELECT driver_id, CAST(julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(ride_date)) AS INTEGER) AS days_idle FROM rides GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Late-night rides
context: Pickups between 23:00 and 03:59.
task: Return ride_id and pickup_time where the pickup hour is 23, 0, 1, 2 or 3.
answer: SELECT ride_id, pickup_time FROM rides WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) IN (23, 0, 1, 2, 3);
